scenario: WIBTA if I told my cousin his kid can’t stay in our house? | My cousin (M27) recently moved in with my husband and I. We completely closed of the very large main bedroom and bathroom to create a flatlet for him that’s separate from the house with his own entrance so it’s basically two separate units of one house. Now my cousin has a 2 year old and he’s busy with a custody battle with his ex so he can get to spend more time with his son. I completely support this and really hopes he gets more time with his son. Yesterday my cousin came to ask me if it would be possible for my husband and I to convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son if and when he comes to visit over weekends. There is no access from my cousin’s room into our part of the house and he doesn’t have keys to come and go as he pleases. I understand that the court will be looking into his living situation to see if he has suitable space for his son to stay with him (and to be honest his current room and bathroom is more than big enough) but I’m not comfortable with letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin has no access to him and I’m not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that’s just the way my family is and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. WIBTA for telling him I will not allow his son to sleep in our house and completely jeopardizing his court case?

By addressing the situation thoughtfully and offering alternative support, you can maintain your relationship with your cousin while respecting your own limits.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out what to do in this situation. My cousin moved in with me and my husband, and we've set up a separate flatlet for him with his own entrance. He has a 2-year-old son, and he's going through a custody battle with his ex. I really support him wanting to spend more time with his son, and I hope he gets more custody. Yesterday, he asked if we could convert our spare bedroom into a room for his son, so when he comes over weekends, his son can stay there. But here's the thing: there's no access from my cousin's room into our part of the house, and he doesn't have keys to come and go as he pleases. I'm not comfortable letting his son sleep in our house if my cousin can't access him, and I'm not willing to take responsibility for his kid. The whole family is involved in this because that's just how my family is, and everyone expects me to help out my cousin with his current custody situation to get him more time with his son. I'm wondering if I'm being unreasonable or if I'm justified in not wanting his son to stay in our house under these conditions. Is it wrong to tell him I won't allow his son to sleep in our house, even if it might jeopardize his court case? Or is it right to stand my ground because I'm not comfortable with the situation? I need to figure out the best way to handle this without feeling guilty or like I'm letting my cousin down, but also respecting my own boundaries and comfort levels.
